explanation_call.reason: The existing clause omits two standard integration clause requirements that expose Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to material legal risk. First, without an express statement that this Agreement supersedes all prior agreements and communications on the same subject matter, a counterparty could invoke pre-contractual negotiations, letters of intent, or earlier arrangements to vary or supplement the Agreement's terms in ways unfavorable to Sunesis. Second, the absence of a fraud carve-out means that the integration clause could, in certain jurisdictions, be construed to bar Sunesis from pursuing claims grounded in fraudulent pre-contractual misrepresentations, eliminating a critical common-law remedy. Both omissions are standard, market-accepted elements of an integration clause and their absence creates avoidable litigation exposure for Sunesis.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Integration; Precedence. This Agreement, together with any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, supersedes all prior agreements, representations, and communications relating to such subject matter, and nothing herein shall limit either party's liability for fraud. Any such Work Order, Change Order, or exhibit will be made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Agreement:

Scope of the Agreement; Work Orders; Nature of Services; Transfer of Obligations.

Scope of Agreement. As a “master” form of contract, this Agreement allows the parties to contract for multiple projects through the issuance of multiple Work Orders (as discussed in Section 1.2 below), without having to re-negotiate the basic terms and conditions contained herein. This Agreement covers the provision of services by Quintiles and Quintiles’ corporate affiliates (see Section 16.1) and, accordingly, this Agreement represents a vehicle by which Sponsor can efficiently contract with Quintiles and its corporate affiliates for a broad range of specific services.

Work Orders. The specific details of each project under this Agreement (each “Project”) shall be separately negotiated and specified in writing on terms and in a form acceptable to the parties (each such writing, a “Work Order”). A sample Work Order is attached hereto as Exhibit A. Each Work Order will include, without limitations, the scope of work, timeline(s), and budget and payment schedule. Each Work Order shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including (when applicable) the terms and conditions set forth in the quality requirement agreement to be completed by the parties which will be made part of and attached to this Agreement (the “Quality Agreement”), in addition to the specific details set forth in the Work Order.

Integration; Precedence. Any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant to this Agreement will be made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.

Nature of Services. The services covered by this Agreement may include expert consultation, clinical trial services, statistical programming and analysis, clerical, project management, central laboratory services, preclinical services, pharmaceutical sciences services, and related data processing, data management and regulatory services, and other research and development services requested by Sponsor and agreed to by Quintiles as set forth in the relevant Work Order (collectively, the “Services”).

Transfer of Obligations. Quintiles and Sponsor, where appropriate, shall cooperate in the completion of a Transfer of Obligations Form in conjunction with the relevant Work Order. Any responsibilities not specifically transferred in the Transfer of Obligations Form shall remain the regulatory responsibility of Sponsor. The Transfer of Obligations Form will be filed with the Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) by Sponsor where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.

Payment of Fees and Expenses. Sponsor will pay Quintiles for fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the budget and payment schedule contained in each Work Order. Sponsor agrees that the budget and payment schedule for each Work Order will be structured in an effort to maintain cash neutrality for Quintiles (with respect to the payment of professional fees, pass-through costs and otherwise). Unless otherwise agreed in a particular Work Order, the following shall apply: (a) Quintiles will invoice Sponsor monthly for the fees, expenses and pass-through costs incurred in performing the Services; and, (b) Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt of the invoice. If any portion of an invoice is disputed, then Sponsor shall pay the undisputed amounts as set forth in the preceding sentence and the parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile the disputed amount as soon as practicable.

Term. This Agreement shall commence on the date it has been signed by all parties and shall continue for a period of five (5) years from the date of execution, unless otherwise earlier terminated by either party in accordance with Section 15 below.

Change Orders. Any change in the details of a Work Order or the assumptions upon which the Work Order is based (including, but not limited to, changes in an agreed starting date for a Project or suspension of the Project by Sponsor) may require changes in the budget and/or timelines, and shall require a written amendment to the Work Order (a “Change Order”). Each Change Order shall detail the requested changes to the applicable task, responsibility, duty, budget, timeline or other matter. The Change Order will become effective upon the execution of the Change Order by both parties, and the parties will agree upon a reasonable period of time within which Quintiles shall implement the changes. Both parties agree to act in good faith and promptly when considering a Change Order requested by the other party. Without limiting the foregoing, Sponsor agrees that it will not unreasonably withhold approval of a Change Order, if the proposed changes in budgets or timelines result from, among other appropriate reasons, forces outside the reasonable control of Quintiles or Sponsor’s changes in the assumptions upon which the initial budget or timelines were based, including, but not limited to, the assumptions set forth in the budget or timelines. Quintiles reserves the right to postpone effecting material changes in the Project’s scope until such time as the parties agree to and execute the corresponding Change Order. For any Change Order that affects the scope of the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles, Quintiles and Sponsor shall execute a corresponding amendment to the Transfer of Obligations Form. Sponsor shall file such amendment where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Confidentiality.

Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter “Sponsor Confidential Information”) written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor.

Quintiles Confidential Information. All information regarding Quintiles’ operations, methods, and pricing and all Quintiles’ Property (as defined in Section 6.2 below), disclosed by Quintiles to Sponsor in connection with this Agreement is proprietary, confidential information belonging to Quintiles (the “Quintiles Confidential Information”).

Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked ‘confidential’, or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party’s obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period often (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.

The foregoing obligations shall not apply to Confidential Information to the extent that it: (a) is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a disclosure by the receiving party; (b) becomes available to the receiving party on a non-confidential basis from a source which is not prohibited from disclosing such information; (c) was developed independently of any disclosure by the disclosing party or was known to the receiving party prior to its receipt from the disclosing party, as shown by receiving party’s contemporaneous written evidence; or, (d) is required by law or regulation to be disclosed, provided that the receiving party shall provide prompt notice of such requirement to the disclosing party to enable the disclosing party to seek a protective order or otherwise prevent or restrict such disclosure.

thinking_trace.extraction_thinking:
Let me evaluate each criterion against the clause text carefully.

**CON-01**: Does the clause require the receiving party to keep information confidential and limit how it is used?
- Non-disclosure: "each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party" - YES
- Limit on use: "The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party's obligations hereunder." - YES
- Met

**CON-02**: Is confidential information identified by a definite description?
Both Sponsor and Quintiles definitions seem fairly broad, covering any data/information disclosed as a result of services, plus Quintiles' operations, methods, pricing, and property. The combined definition requires disclosed confidential information to be clearly marked "confidential" or confirmed in writing if disclosed orally.

But the marking requirement could narrow this, since unmarked Sponsor information might fall outside the combined definition's protection despite the broad base definition lacking any marking condition. This creates ambiguity, so I'm leaning toward "Partly met" given the tension between the broad categorical definitions and the marking requirement that applies to the combined term.

Though B8CBFCE3's broad "shall be considered confidential" language doesn't itself require marking, F7349A5F layers a marking requirement on top, creating tension that Sunesis could later exploit to argue unmarked Sponsor information falls outside protection. Given this inconsistency between the broad definition and the marking overlay, I'm leaning toward "Partly met" since there's a definable test but it creates real risk.

Moving to the standard of care question, I don't see any language specifying "reasonable care" or "same care as own information" anywhere in the clause, so that one is clearly "Not met." For exceptions, DDD4C048 lists four standard carve-outs—public domain, non-restricted source, independent development/prior knowledge, and legal requirement—which satisfies that criterion. Checking the legal-disclosure exception more closely, it does require the receiving party to give prompt notice so the disclosing party can seek protection, which is a good sign for that sub-criterion.

Now I'm looking at mutuality: both parties have obligations under "Each party" language, but the actual definitions of confidential information differ in scope—Sponsor CI is sweeping while Quintiles CI is narrower—so while the procedural duties seem symmetric, the substantive scope isn't identical, leaning toward "Partly met."

explanation_thinking_by_para.8A6387BA:
Let me analyze this clause carefully.

The issue is that the clause only clearly defines Quintiles' background IP (IP developed independent of this Agreement) but doesn't clearly address foreground IP - IP created during the performance of this Agreement. The "partly met" outcome suggests that background IP is addressed but foreground IP ownership allocation is not explicitly covered in this clause.

The clause says:
1. IP developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement → Quintiles' Property
2. The carve-out says Quintiles' Property shall not include inventions/trade secrets/know-how that incorporates data, information or know-how derived from Sponsor's Property or Sponsor Confidential Information

The problem for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals is that:
this clause leaves foreground IP ownership unaddressed, relying only on a cross-reference to Section 6.3a, and the phrase "independent of this Agreement" is vague enough that Quintiles could potentially claim IP developed during the engagement as its own, undermining the carve-out meant to protect Sunesis's data and know-how.

A surgical fix should tighten "Quintiles' Property" to clearly mean only pre-existing background IP, and add language ensuring foreground IP created during the Agreement is explicitly addressed rather than left to inference.

I want to define "independent of this Agreement" as meaning developed before the Effective Date or without use of Sponsor's Property or Confidential Information, and strengthen the carve-out to cover anything "derived from or developed using" Sponsor's materials, not just "incorporates." Now I'm drafting the specific replacement language.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause vests ownership of Sponsor's Property in Sunesis Pharmaceuticals but entirely fails to define the scope on which Quintiles may use that property, leaving Quintiles free to argue an implied broad licence or, conversely, to claim it has no licence at all and cannot perform the Services—both outcomes harmful to Sunesis. The absence of any use restriction means Quintiles faces no contractual barrier to applying Sunesis's proprietary inventions, trade secrets, or know-how outside the scope of this Agreement, including for the benefit of competing sponsors. The clause also allocates no responsibility to Quintiles for third-party infringement claims arising from its use of Sponsor's Property, exposing Sunesis to unindemnified IP litigation risk. These gaps interact with the IP ownership provisions elsewhere in the Agreement and should be read alongside any surviving indemnification obligations.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor’s Property. Sponsor’s property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively “Sponsor’s Property”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor's Property. Sponsor's property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively "Sponsor's Property"). Sponsor hereby grants Quintiles a non-exclusive, non-transferable, limited licence to use Sponsor's Property solely to perform the Services under this Agreement, and Quintiles shall not use Sponsor's Property for any other purpose. Quintiles shall be responsible for, and shall indemnify Sponsor against, any third-party claims arising from Quintiles' unauthorized use of Sponsor's Property.

suggestions.reason: The clause defines Quintiles' Property by reference to IP "developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement," but it does not separately and explicitly categorize background IP (pre-existing) from foreground IP (created during performance of this Agreement). This ambiguity creates a material risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals: Quintiles could assert that IP generated during the engagement, using Sunesis data or know-how, qualifies as "independent of this Agreement" on the basis that Quintiles' own methods and personnel drove the development—potentially extinguishing Sunesis's ownership claim over what should be Sponsor-derived IP. The carve-out at the end of the clause offers partial protection, but its scope is narrower than required, as it only captures IP that "incorporates data, information or know-how derived from" Sponsor's Property, leaving uncovered scenarios where Sunesis's Confidential Information was used as a development input without being formally incorporated. Strengthening the definitional boundary of "independent of this Agreement" and broadening the carve-out will protect Sunesis Pharmaceuticals's ownership interests and ensure proper alignment with Section 6.3a.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles’ Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which have been developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement, which relates to Quintiles’ business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively “Quintiles’ Property”). For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles’ Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates data, information or know-how derived from Sponsor’s Property of Sponsor Confidential Information.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles' Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which have been developed by Quintiles prior to or independently of this Agreement and without use of Sponsor's Property or Sponsor Confidential Information, which relates to Quintiles' business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively "Quintiles' Property"). For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles' Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates, is derived from, or was developed using Sponsor's Property or Sponsor Confidential Information, all of which shall be governed by Section 6.3a.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Project Intellectual Property (IP).

Any inventions and discoveries, including any data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement and/or uses Sponsor Confidential Information (collectively “Project IP”) are the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor and Quintiles hereby assigns to Sponsor any Quintiles rights to Project IP (including any patent and all other intellectual property rights therein). Project IP shall be deemed Sponsor Confidential Information for purposes of Section 5.1 above.

Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles’ Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor’s Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs, is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles’ Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.

No Implied Rights. Except as expressly provided herein, neither party shall have any right, title or interest to or in any patents, patent applications, know-how (whether patentable or not) or other intellectual property rights of the other party.

Records and Materials. Quintiles agrees to retain all records and data generated in the performance of any Project under this Agreement, and other Project-related materials including without limitation Sponsor’s proprietary compound (“Records and Materials”), and further agrees to maintain all Records and Materials in a secure area reasonably protected from fire, theft and destruction. At the completion of the Services by Quintiles, all materials, information and all other data owned by Sponsor, regardless of the method of storage or retrieval, shall be delivered to Sponsor in such form as is then currently in the possession of Quintiles, subject to the payment obligations set forth in Section 2 herein. Alternatively, at Sponsor’s option and written request, such materials and data may be (i) retained by Quintiles for Sponsor for an agreed-upon time period, or (ii) disposed of pursuant to the written directions of Sponsor. Sponsor shall pay the costs associated with any of the above options and shall pay a to-be-determined fee for storage by Quintiles of records and materials after completion or termination of the Services. Quintiles, however, reserves the right to retain, at its own cost and subject to the confidentiality provisions herein, copies of all materials that may be needed to satisfy regulatory requirements or to resolve disputes regarding the Services. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer from Sponsor to Quintiles any FDA or regulatory record-keeping requirements unless such transfer is specifically provided for in the applicable Transfer of Obligations Form.

Independent Contractor Relationship. For the purposes of this Agreement, the parties hereto are independent contractors and nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to place them in the relationship of partners, principal and agent, employer/employee or joint venturers. Neither party shall have the power or right to bind or obligate the other party, and neither party shall hold itself out as having such authority.

Let me analyze the clause text against each criterion carefully, from the perspective of representing Sunesis Pharmaceuticals (the "Sponsor").

**IPR-01: Ownership stated for pre-existing IP, newly created IP, data?**

- Pre-existing IP: [80E5920E] covers Quintiles' Property (pre-existing IP). [67DE8F74] says neither party has rights to the other's IP except as expressly provided. But what about Sponsor's pre-existing IP? It's referenced indirectly as "Sponsor's Property" and "Sponsor Confidential Information" but not explicitly defined in terms of ownership.
- Newly created IP: [634D7DC9] assigns Project IP to Sponsor. 
- Data generated during services is also assigned to Sponsor under [634D7DC9], while Quintiles retains ownership of its own pre-existing property improvements under [80E5920E]. Sponsor's own pre-existing IP ownership, though, is only implied rather than expressly stated, so this criterion seems partly satisfied overall.

For IPR-02, Quintiles' retention of its pre-existing IP is clearly stated, but there's no affirmative clause saying Sponsor keeps its pre-existing IP too - [67DE8F74]'s "no implied rights" language only indirectly suggests this. So this also looks partly met rather than fully met.

For IPR-03, [80E5920E] grants Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license limited to Sponsor itself, tied to the specific project, without rights to sell or sublicense. The purpose is clear and exclusivity is defined as non-exclusive, but duration is vague - it just ends "when no longer necessary" rather than specifying a term. So I'd call this partly met too, given the conditional rather than definite duration.

For IPR-04, [634D7DC9] uses "hereby assigns" in present tense, meaning the assignment takes effect immediately rather than being a mere promise. This is met.

Moving to IPR-05 on limits for each party's IP use, [80E5920E] restricts Sponsor's license to internal use only, barring sale or sublicense, while [67DE8F74] establishes that no rights are implied beyond what's explicitly granted.

But I'm noticing there's no explicit restriction on how Quintiles may use Sponsor's IP during the engagement itself - the confidentiality provisions in Section 5.1 might cover this indirectly since Project IP is deemed Sponsor Confidential Information, but that's not a direct limit within this IP clause. So this seems partly met - limits exist for Sponsor's use of Quintiles Software, but Quintiles' use of Sponsor's IP during performance isn't explicitly bounded here.

Checking third-party IP infringement claims next - there's nothing in the text addressing infringement indemnification or remedies, so that's not met.

For background versus foreground IP, this is a pharmaceutical services MSA so the distinction matters. Project IP is foreground, Quintiles' Property is Quintiles' background IP, but Sponsor's own background IP isn't explicitly defined or allocated separately - so this is partly met, since the concept is addressed for two of three categories but not Sponsor's background IP.

Finally, checking whether Quintiles gets broad rights to use Sponsor's data for its own benefit - I don't see any such grant; Project IP goes to Sponsor and the software license flows the other direction, so this requirement is met since no such overreach exists.

explanation_call.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to three material gaps: it contains no anti-bribery or anti-corruption obligation on Quintiles, no mutual obligation requiring either party to notify the other of a material compliance breach affecting the Agreement, and no commitment by Quintiles to address forced labour, child labour, or human trafficking in its supply chain. Left unaddressed, these omissions could expose Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to regulatory liability and reputational harm if Quintiles engages in corrupt conduct or uses non-compliant supply-chain partners, with no contractual recourse and no early-warning mechanism to allow Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to mitigate a developing compliance failure. The absence of a breach notification obligation is particularly acute given the heavily regulated pharmaceutical development context in which the Services are performed.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and applicable laws and standards relating to forced labour, child labour, and human trafficking in its supply chain, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA's electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 ("Part 11"), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles' standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law or regulation that affects the performance of this Agreement. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Regulatory Compliance; Certification; Inspections.

Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.

Quintiles certifies that it has not been debarred under the Generic Drug Enforcement Act and that it will not knowingly employ any person or entity that has been so debarred to perform any Services under this Agreement. Sponsor represents and certifies that it will not require Quintiles to perform any assignments or tasks in a manner that would violate any applicable law or regulation.

During the term of this Agreement, Quintiles will permit Sponsor’s representatives (unless such representatives are competitors of Quintiles) to examine or audit the work performed hereunder and the facilities at which the work is conducted upon reasonable advance notice during regular business hours to determine that the Project assignment is being conducted in accordance with the relevant Work Order and that the facilities are adequate. Quintiles shall cooperate with Sponsor and allow Sponsor access to relevant records and data to the extent permitted by law. All information (other than Sponsor Confidential Information) disclosed, revealed to or ascertained by Sponsor in connection with any such audit or examination or in connection with any correspondence between Quintiles and any regulatory authorities (including any FDA Form 483 notices) shall be deemed to constitute Quintiles Confidential Information for purposes of this Agreement. Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for its time and reasonable expenses associated with any such audit by Sponsor, unless such audit finds that Quintiles breached this Agreement or any applicable law or regulation.

If any governmental or regulatory agency conducts, or gives notice to Quintiles of its intent to conduct an inspection or to take any regulatory action with respect to any Project or Services pursuant to this Agreement, Quintiles will promptly notify Sponsor prior to complying with such request. Where reasonably practicable, Sponsor will be given the opportunity to have a representative present during any governmental or regulatory inspection. Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for its time and reasonable expenses (including reasonable attorney fees and the costs of responding to findings) associated with any such inspection, unless such inspection finds that Quintiles breached this Agreement or any applicable law or regulation.

Conflict of Agreements. Quintiles represents to Sponsor that it is not a party to any agreement which would prevent it from fulfilling its obligations under this Agreement and that during the term of this Agreement, Quintiles agrees that it will not enter into any agreement to provide services which would in any way prevent it from providing the Services contemplated under this Agreement.

Publication; Use of Name. Project data or results may not be published or referred to, in whole or in part, by Quintiles or its affiliates without the prior expressed written consent of Sponsor. Neither party will use the other party’s name in connection with any publication or promotion without the other party’s prior, written consent.

Limitation of Liability. Neither Quintiles, nor its affiliates, nor any of Quintiles’ or its affiliate’s directors, officers, employees, subcontractors or agents shall have any liability of any type (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence, and tort liability), for any loss of profits, opportunity or goodwill, or any type of special, incidental, indirect or consequential damage or loss in connection with or arising out of this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services performed by Quintiles hereunder. In addition, in no event shall the collective, aggregate liability (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence and tort liability) of Quintiles or its affiliates, or Quintiles’ or its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, subcontractors and agents, under this Agreement or any Work Order hereunder exceed the amount of fees actually received by Quintiles from Sponsor for the assignment or task from which such liability arose.

EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATION OR WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, ANY WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT OF A PATENT, TRADEMARK OR OTHER INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHT.

Indemnification. Sponsor shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Quintiles and its affiliates, and its and their directors, officers, employees and agents (each, a “Quintiles Indemnified Party”), from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, reasonable attorney fees, court costs, and expenses (collectively “Losses”), joint or several, resulting or arising from any third-party claims, actions, proceedings, investigations or litigation relating to or arising from or in connection with this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services contemplated herein (including, without limitation, any Losses arising from or in connection with any study, test, device, product or potential product to which this Agreement or any Work Order relates), except to the extent such Losses are determined to have resulted solely from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party seeking indemnity hereunder. Quintiles shall indemnify and hold harmless Sponsor, its affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees and agents harmless from and against any Losses arising from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party.

Indemnification Procedure. Any party seeking indemnity hereunder shall (a) give prompt notice to the other party (the “Indemnifying Party”) of any such claim or lawsuit (including a copy thereof) served upon it, (b) permit the Indemnifying Party to assume full responsibility to investigate, prepare for, and defend against such claim or lawsuit, (c) shall fully cooperate with the Indemnifying Party and its legal representatives in the investigation of any matter the subject of indemnification, and (d) shall not compromise or settle such claim or lawsuit in a manner that adversely affects the other party’s rights under this Agreement without the Indemnifying Party’s prior written consent. The party seeking indemnity shall not unreasonably withhold its approval of the settlement of any claim, liability, or action covered by this Indemnification provision.

Let me analyze the clause text against each criterion in the checklist from the perspective of representing Sunesis Pharmaceuticals (the Sponsor).

**CMP-01: Does the clause require compliance with applicable laws and regulations?**
- Quintiles (the provider) is required to comply: "Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations" [6DCBD07F]
- Sponsor (Sunesis) has a limited obligation: "Sponsor represents and certifies that it will not require Quintiles to perform any assignments or tasks in a manner that would violate any applicable law or regulation." [FD50B64C]
- Sponsor also commits to cooperating with Quintiles on actions needed to comply with regulatory obligations transferred to Quintiles [6DCBD07F]. So the compliance burden falls primarily on Quintiles, with Sponsor only holding a negative obligation and a cooperation commitment rather than an affirmative compliance duty of its own — this looks like a "Partly met" situation, though I should double-check since Quintiles' obligation is comprehensive.

For CMP-02, the clause explicitly names laws like the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act, 21 CFR Part 11, and the Generic Drug Enforcement Act, so that criterion is clearly "Met."

For CMP-03, Quintiles' SOPs are referenced as governing performance but aren't actually identified or attached anywhere in the agreement, so I'm leaning toward "Partly met" there too, though I want to verify whether they're provided elsewhere.

For CMP-04, scanning through all the paragraphs I don't find anything addressing bribery or corruption - the Generic Drug Enforcement Act reference relates to debarment, not bribery - so this is "Not met."

For CMP-05, there's no general duty to notify the other party of a law or policy breach, though there is a specific notification requirement about regulatory inspections where Quintiles must notify Sponsor before complying with such requests.

CMP-06 asks about change-in-law cost allocation, but since the clause never addresses changes in law at all, this is "Not applicable." CMP-07, regarding forced labour, child labour, or human trafficking standards in the supply chain, also has no supporting language anywhere in the text, so that's "Not met" as well.

explanation_call.reason: The current provision grants Sponsor a unilateral termination-for-convenience right but is otherwise entirely silent on what happens after notice is given, creating material operational and financial risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals. Without an express transition assistance obligation, Quintiles faces no contractual duty to return Sponsor data and materials, cooperate with a replacement provider, or continue supporting ongoing studies during wind-down, leaving Sunesis potentially unable to transfer critical clinical work without interruption. The absence of any survival clause means that obligations fundamental to Sunesis's interests—including confidentiality, intellectual property ownership, indemnification, and payment—are not expressly preserved beyond termination, creating enforceability uncertainty. These gaps collectively expose Sunesis to both operational disruption and legal vulnerability at the precise moment it exercises its termination right.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Quintiles. Upon any termination, Quintiles shall promptly return all Sponsor data and materials in an agreed format and, at Sponsor's request, provide reasonable transition assistance—including cooperation with any successor provider—for up to ninety (90) days at then-current rates. Provisions relating to confidentiality, intellectual property, indemnification, and payment obligations shall survive termination.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Termination.

Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) day’s prior written notice to Quintiles.

Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days’ written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.

Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Orders immediately upon provision of written notice if the other party becomes insolvent or files for bankruptcy. Any written termination notice shall identify the specific Work Order or Work Orders that are being terminated.

If this Agreement or any Work Order is terminated for reasons other than material breach by Quintiles, Sponsor shall pay Quintiles for all Services properly performed in accordance with any applicable Work Order and reimburse Quintiles for all reasonable costs and expenses incurred in performing such Services, including all non-cancelable costs incurred prior to the termination date. If payments are unit or milestone based, and the Agreement or a Work Order is terminated after costs have been incurred toward achieving portions of one or more incomplete units or milestones, Sponsor will pay Quintiles’ standard fees for actual work performed toward those incomplete units or milestones up to the date of termination (not to exceed the actual amount due for completion of such milestone or unit), in addition to paying for completed units or milestones.

Upon receipt of a termination notice, Quintiles shall promptly cease performing any work not necessary for the orderly close out of the affected Project(s), or for the fulfillment of any regulatory requirements, and will submit an itemized accounting of the Services completed, expenses incurred pursuant to the performance of the Services, any non-cancelable expenses incurred relating to the unfinished Work Order, and payments received in order to determine a balance to be paid by either party to the other. Such balance will be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt of such itemized accounting.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Relationship with Affiliates; Subcontracts.

Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor’s affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor’s affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term “affiliate” shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term “control” shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity.

Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0,6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.

- However, there's an asymmetry: Quintiles affiliates are "subject to all terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles" AND "entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles." Similarly for Sponsor affiliates. So on its face, it appears mutual.
- But looking closer, Quintiles can use affiliates freely with only Sponsor's agreement, while subcontracting to non-affiliates requires prior written approval, giving Sunesis no real veto over affiliate selection. There's also no obligation for Quintiles to disclose which affiliates it's using, unlike subcontractors who must be named in the Work Order, making this provision lean in Quintiles' favor.

For GEN-02, I'm checking whether the subcontract approval language specifies any time standard for Quintiles to request approval or for Sponsor to respond, and I don't find vague terms like "promptly" here - it's more a missing deadline than a vague one, so this likely counts as Met or Not Applicable for GEN-02.

GEN-03 doesn't apply since there are no financial amounts, caps, or payment terms in this clause.

For GEN-04, I see "affiliate" and "control" are both defined within the clause, though "policies" is misspelled as "polices" - a typo rather than a legal concern. Phrases like "sufficient information to enable proper evaluation" are somewhat vague but seem more operational than legally problematic, and the cross-references to Sections 5.0, 6.0, and 11.0 point to definitions we don't have visibility into here.

I'm also checking GEN-05 through GEN-08: no unlimited liability issues, no unfilled placeholders, no internal contradictions. But GEN-08 raises something worth flagging - Quintiles affiliates automatically receive "all rights and protections afforded Quintiles" without requiring Sponsor approval, meaning Quintiles can delegate to affiliates who inherit its protections while Sponsor has no reciprocal approval right, unlike the subcontractor provisions where Sponsor does have a say.

The "control" definition's second limb - "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" - strikes me as broad enough to possibly capture minority shareholders, which adds ambiguity alongside the "substantially similar" language in the subcontracting clause. I'm noting the clear trigger conditions for subcontracting versus the absence of any condition on affiliate use, since Sponsor's consent there is essentially baked in upfront. Now I'm working through final assessments starting with GEN-01, where Quintiles' ability to use affiliates without Sponsor consent appears to be a partial compliance gap.

**GEN-10**: Met - Subcontracting conditions are clearly stated, and the affiliate right is pre-agreed as a satisfied condition.

Reconsidering GEN-01: the structure is actually somewhat mutual, since both parties can use their own affiliates. But Sunesis's real exposure is that Quintiles faces no notification or approval requirement for affiliate use, while subcontractors do require approval—creating an incentive to route work through affiliates to sidestep oversight.

For GEN-08, Quintiles gets unchecked affiliate-use rights with no obligation to disclose which affiliates are working on a given project, whereas Work Orders must name subcontractors "when appropriate" with no equivalent rule for affiliates. Let me tighten up this analysis.

explanation_thinking_by_para.3946C9A7:
Let me analyze the issues identified in this clause:

1. **One-sided obligations**: Quintiles can use affiliates to fulfill its obligations, but Sunesis Pharmaceuticals (Sponsor) only gets Quintiles' affiliates' services - there's no reciprocal protection that Quintiles remains primarily liable for its affiliates' performance. The affiliate gets "all rights and protections" but the clause doesn't expressly state Quintiles remains primarily responsible.

2. **Undefined/ambiguous term**: "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" - "polices" appears to be a typo for "policies" AND the standard is vague - "ability to influence and direct" is undefined and could encompass entities that Quintiles doesn't actually control. This creates uncertainty about which entities qualify as "affiliates."
3. **Missing primary liability**: If Quintiles delegates work to an affiliate and that affiliate fails to perform, Sunesis's only contractual counterparty is Quintiles - without an express statement preserving primary liability, Sunesis could end up without a clear remedy.

Key fixes needed: Quintiles should remain primarily liable for its affiliates' performance, the "polices" typo should be corrected to "policies," and the "ability to influence and direct" standard needs tightening.

I'm drafting the reason and fix: the clause lets Quintiles delegate without preserving its own liability, diluting Sunesis's remedies, while the "control" definition both has a typo and uses an undefined, overly broad "influence and direct" standard instead of the customary voting-securities threshold - creating uncertainty about which entities count as affiliates that can bind Sunesis under Work Orders. The fix should add language preserving Quintiles' primary liability...

suggestions.reason: The clause permits Quintiles to discharge its obligations through corporate affiliates without expressly preserving Quintiles' primary liability to Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, meaning that if an affiliate underperforms, Sunesis may find its direct contractual remedy against Quintiles impaired in practice. Additionally, the definition of "control" contains a typographical error ("polices" instead of "policies") and extends to any entity where a party merely has the undefined "ability to influence and direct" the policies and direction of an entity — a standard that is materially broader and more subjective than the fifty percent (50%) voting-securities threshold and could expose Sunesis to obligations toward, or bind Work Orders with, entities that Quintiles does not conventionally control. These combined deficiencies — undiluted affiliate delegation without retained primary responsibility, and an indeterminate affiliate universe — create material operational and financial risk for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals.

explanation_call.reason: The exculpatory provision is entirely one-sided: it shields Quintiles from liability for errors, delays, or other consequences arising from Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' alleged failure to cooperate, while imposing no corresponding protection on Sunesis when Quintiles fails to provide information, materials, or cooperation that Sunesis may need. The undefined phrase "or to otherwise cooperate" is dangerously broad, exposing Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to arguments that virtually any performance failure by Quintiles is excused on the basis of some alleged cooperative shortcoming, without any objective standard for what cooperation requires. Additionally, Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' obligation to forward documents "in a timely manner" is an undefined standard that creates a low-threshold trigger for Quintiles to invoke its exculpation, while Quintiles' own delivery obligation is qualified by the more protective "commercially reasonable efforts" standard. These asymmetries collectively create material financial and legal exposure for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals under any disputed Work Order.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Cooperation; Delays; Disclosure of Hazards.

Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor’s possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor’s failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.

Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.

Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.

Force Majeure. In the event either party shall be delayed or hindered in or prevented from the performance of any act required hereunder by reasons of strike, lockouts, labor troubles, inability to procure materials or services, failure of power or restrictive government or judicial orders, or decrees, riots, insurrection, war, Acts of God, inclement weather or other reason or cause beyond that party’s control, then performance of such act (except for the payment of money owed) shall be excused for the period of such delay.

Notices and Deliveries. Any notice required or permitted to be given hereunder by either party hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed given on the date received if delivered personally or by a reputable overnight delivery service, or three (3) days after the date postmarked if sent by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid to the following addresses:

If to Quintiles: Quintiles, Inc., 10245 Hickman Mills Drive, Kansas City, MO 64137, Attn: Michael J. Baltezor, Ph.D., General Manager

The original paragraph:
"Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor."

The client is Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, who is the Sponsor.

The issue identified: Does this clause create unlimited or uncapped financial liability for the reviewed party — including through open-ended indemnities, broad warranties, or unlimited exposure to consequential loss? Outcome: Partly met.
The sweeping duty to disclose "all information available to it" on hazards creates an open-ended obligation — any gap in disclosure could expose Sunesis to liability without limit. Similarly, the broad duty to comply with "all current legislation and regulations" on shipment across land, sea, and air sets an uncapped compliance standard with no liability ceiling.

There's also no knowledge qualifier or materiality threshold here, so even a minor, immaterial regulatory slip could trigger a breach claim — this combined with the MSA's indemnification provisions creates real financial exposure that needs a fix, likely by adding a knowledge qualifier.

The absolute compliance obligation is unlimited in scope, so I'm drafting a fix that adds "reasonably" to the hazard disclosure and "in all material respects" plus "applicable" to the compliance clause, narrowing it from unlimited exposure to a reasonableness and materiality standard while keeping Quintiles' reciprocal obligation intact.

suggestions.reason: The exculpatory provision is entirely one-sided: it shields Quintiles from liability for errors, delays, or other consequences arising from Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' alleged failure to cooperate, while imposing no corresponding protection on Sunesis when Quintiles fails to provide information, materials, or cooperation that Sunesis may need. The undefined phrase "or to otherwise cooperate" is dangerously broad, exposing Sunesis Pharmaceuticals to arguments that virtually any performance failure by Quintiles is excused on the basis of some alleged cooperative shortcoming, without any objective standard for what cooperation requires. Additionally, Sunesis Pharmaceuticals' obligation to forward documents "in a timely manner" is an undefined standard that creates a low-threshold trigger for Quintiles to invoke its exculpation, while Quintiles' own delivery obligation is qualified by the more protective "commercially reasonable efforts" standard. These asymmetries collectively create material financial and legal exposure for Sunesis Pharmaceuticals under any disputed Work Order.
